title: Temurah 20
description: Rabbi Shimon’s rule that only an animal with inherent sanctity renders a substitute and the Gemara’s challenges to it, Rabbi Yehoshua’s consecrated possessions and deferred sanctity, then a new mishna on the substitute of a guilt offering and its offspring, and whether the offspring of a female guilt offering may be a burnt offering.
topics: 🐑 Rabbi Shimon: only what grazes until blemished renders a substitute
🍖 Rabbi: a leftover Paschal offering is a peace offering, so a female Paschal offering renders a substitute
🐐 Borrowed status: the red heifer, the king’s goat and “two bodies”
🕊️ Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: a vowed burnt offering may be a bird
🏛️ One who consecrates all his possessions: Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and deferred sanctity
⚖️ Mishna: the substitute of a guilt offering and its offspring graze, die, or buy a burnt offering
✋ An individual’s burnt offering or a communal gift offering: hands, libations, service and hide
❓ Rabba bar Avuh’s two versions, and Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya’s question about a female guilt offering’s offspring
