a2.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָתוֹ — עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה, לְפִסְחוֹ וְלַאֲשָׁמוֹ — אֵין עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה.

a3.he: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, אֶלָּא הָרוֹעֶה לְהִסְתָּאֵב.

a4.he: אָמַר רַבִּי: אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּפֶּסַח, הוֹאִיל וּמוֹתַר הַפֶּסַח קָרֵב שְׁלָמִים.

a5.he: וְלֵימָא: אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּאָשָׁם, הוֹאִיל וּמוֹתַר אָשָׁם קָרֵב עוֹלָה! רַבִּי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבָּנַן, דְּאָמְרִי: מוֹתָרוֹת לְנִדְבַת צִיבּוּר אָזְלִי, וְאֵין תְּמוּרָה בְּצִבּוּר.

a6.he: קָא סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גַּבֵּי מַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָתוֹ, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה, דְּהָאִיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלֶה עָלֶיהָ גַּבֵּי עוֹלַת הָעוֹף.

a7.he: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ פָּרָה לְפָרוֹ — תִּיקְדּוֹשׁ, דְּהָאִיכָּא פָּרַת חַטָּאת! קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הוּא, וְקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לָא עָבְדִי תְּמוּרָה.

a8.he: יָחִיד שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ שָׂעִיר לִשְׂעִירָתוֹ — תִּיקְדּוֹשׁ, דְּהָאִיכָּא שְׂעִיר נָשִׂיא! אִי נָמֵי, נָשִׂיא שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ שְׂעִירָה לִשְׂעִירוֹ — תִּיקְדּוֹשׁ, דְּהָא יָחִיד מַפְרִישׁ שְׂעִירָה!

a10.he: חָטְאוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַנּוּ, כִּי מַפְרֵישׁ שָׂעִיר לִשְׂעִירָתוֹ — תִּיקְדּוֹשׁ, דְּהָא אִילּוּ חָטָא הַשְׁתָּא — בַּר אֵיתוֹיֵי שָׂעִיר הוּא! הָא לָא חָטָא — לָא אִיחַיַּיב בְּשָׂעִיר.

a11.he: אִי הָכִי, הָכָא נָמֵי, הָא לָאו עוֹלַת הָעוֹף קָמַיְיתֵי!

a12.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, דִּתְנַן: ״הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה״ — יָבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: אוֹ תּוֹר אוֹ בְּנֵי יוֹנָה.

a13.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו, וְהָיָה בָּהֶן בְּהֵמָה רְאוּיָה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבוֹת.

a14.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: זְכָרִים יִמָּכְרוּ לְצׇרְכֵי עוֹלוֹת, וּנְקֵבוֹת יִמָּכְרוּ לְצׇרְכֵי שְׁלָמִים, וּדְמֵיהֶן יִפְּלוּ עִם שְׁאָר נְכָסִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

a15.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: זְכָרִים עַצְמָן יִקְרְבוּ עוֹלוֹת, וּנְקֵבוֹת יִמָּכְרוּ לְצׇרְכֵי שְׁלָמִים, וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלוֹת, וּשְׁאָר נְכָסִים יִפְּלוּ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

a16.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּאָמַר זְכָרִים עַצְמָן יִקְרְבוּ עוֹלוֹת, וּנְקֵבוֹת הֵיכִי (מקרבן) [קָרְבָן] שְׁלָמִים? הָא מִכֹּחַ קְדוּשָּׁה דְּחוּיָּיה קָאָתְיָין!

a17.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ זְכָרִים עַצְמָן יִקְרְבוּ עוֹלוֹת, לְמֵימְרָא דִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף אַקְדְּשִׁינְהוּ? אִי הָכִי, נְקֵבוֹת אַמַּאי יִמָּכְרוּ לְצׇרְכֵי שְׁלָמִים? בָּעֲיָא רְעִיָּיה!

a18.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: כֹּל מִידֵּי דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ לְגוּפֵיהּ — לָא נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף. דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תִּמָּכֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּמוּם, וְאָמְרִינַן דְּטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — כֵּיוָן דְּלָא חַזְיָא נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם, לָא נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

a19.he: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גַּבֵּי נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם,

b1.he: דְּלֵיכָּא שֵׁם אָשָׁם עַל אִמּוֹ, אֲבָל גַּבֵּי נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָה דְּאִיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה!

b2.he: וְעוֹד, הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לְעוֹלָתוֹ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה!

b3.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אַף לְעוֹלָתוֹ אֵין עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.

b4.he: מַתְנִי׳ תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם, וְלַד תְּמוּרָה, וְלָדָן וְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם — יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ, וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיִפְּלוּ (דָּמָיו) [דְּמֵיהֶן] לִנְדָבָה. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יָמוּתוּ. וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: יָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהּ עוֹלוֹת.

b5.he: אָשָׁם שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלָיו, וְשֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלָיו — יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ, וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיִפְּלוּ דָּמָיו לִנְדָבָה. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יָמוּתוּ. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: יָבִיא בְּדָמֶיהָ עוֹלָה.

b6.he: וַהֲלֹא אַף נְדָבָה עוֹלָה הִיא, וּמָה בֵּין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים? אֶלָּא, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה עוֹלָה — סוֹמֵךְ עָלֶיהָ, וּמֵבִיא נְסָכִים, וּנְסָכֶיהָ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ. אִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן — עֲבוֹדָתָהּ וְעוֹרָהּ שֶׁלּוֹ.

b7.he: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהִיא נְדָבָה — אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ עָלֶיהָ, וְאֵינוֹ מֵבִיא עָלֶיהָ נְסָכִים, וּנְסָכֶיהָ מִשֶּׁל צִיבּוּר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא כֹּהֵן — עֲבוֹדָתָהּ וְעוֹרָהּ מִשֶּׁל אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר.

b9.he: דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן אָשָׁם, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר יָמוּתוּ, מִשּׁוּם דְּגָזַר לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה.

b10.he: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם, וְלַד תְּמוּרָתָהּ, אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן.

b11.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָתָם, בְּהָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן, אֲבָל גַּבֵּי אָשָׁם מוֹדוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר — צְרִיכָא.

b12.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: מַחְלוֹקֶת לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה, אֲבָל לִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הוּא עַצְמוֹ יִקְרַב אָשָׁם.

b13.he: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר, חֲדָא דְּאֵין אָדָם מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּדָבָר הַבָּא בַּעֲבֵירָה, וְעוֹד, הָתָנֵי רַב חֲנַנְיָא לְסַיּוֹעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי דְּאָמַר וָלָד רִאשׁוֹן קָרֵב, וְלַד שֵׁנִי אֵינוֹ קָרֵב!

b14.he: אֶלָּא, אִי אִיתְּמַר, הָכִי אִיתְּמַר: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: מַחְלוֹקֶת קוֹדֶם כַּפָּרָה, אֲבָל לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה — הוּא עַצְמוֹ קָרֵב עוֹלָה.

b15.he: וְהָתָנֵי רַב חֲנַנְיָא לְסַיּוֹעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי! קַשְׁיָא.

b16.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר חִיָּיא מֵרַבִּי אָבִין בַּר כָּהֲנָא: הִפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם, בְּנָהּ מַהוּ שֶׁיִּקְרַב לְעוֹלָה? וְתִיפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, דְּאָמַר: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר. לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ.

b17.he: מַאי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנָהּ קָרֵב עוֹלָה. הַאי מַאי? עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֶלָּא מַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָה, דְּאִיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ, אֲבָל גַּבֵּי אָשָׁם דְּלֵיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מוֹדֶה!

b18.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּשֵׁם עוֹלֶה עַל אִמּוֹ, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲזֵי לְהַקְרָבָה, וְהָא נָמֵי חֲזֵי לְהַקְרָבָה.

b19.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: וְלָדָן וְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם יָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלָה — בִּדְמֵיהֶן — אִין,

messages.text: Continued from 19b: a baraita taught that one who consecrates a female animal for his burnt offering,

or for his Paschal offering or for his guilt offering, although these offerings are brought only from male animals, it is still consecrated with inherent sanctity. Therefore, if one exchanges for it a non-sacred animal, he renders that animal a substitute, which is consecrated with the same sanctity as the original animal.

notes.he: לא מצינו אשם ופסח נקבה:
notes.en: For his Paschal offering and for his guilt offering: we have not found a female guilt offering or a female Paschal offering.

messages.text: The halakha is not the same in all these cases. Granted, if he consecrates a female animal for his burnt offering, it renders the non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute, as there is burnt offering status for female birds. For this reason it is consecrated with inherent sanctity and can be sold only after it has become blemished.

notes.he: דהויין חובתו אין עושה תמורה דלא קדשה אלא לדמיה שאין לך דבר שעושה תמורה אלא דבר הרועה ומסתאב אותו שיש בו כל כך קדושה בו שצריך רעייה עושין תמורה אבל מפריש נקבה לאשם הואיל וסבירא ליה דתימכר שלא במום וה"ה מפריש נקבה לפסחו הילכך אין עושין תמורה:
notes.en: For his Paschal offering and for his guilt offering, which are his obligation, it does not render a substitute, since it is consecrated only for its value. For nothing renders a substitute except something that grazes and becomes blemished: what has so much sanctity in it that it requires grazing renders a substitute. But one who designates a female for a guilt offering, since [Rabbi Shimon] holds that it is sold without a blemish, and likewise one who designates a female for his Paschal offering, therefore they do not render a substitute.

messages.text: But if he consecrates a female animal for his Paschal offering or for his guilt offering it is not consecrated with inherent sanctity, and it may be sold even without a blemish. Therefore, it does not render the non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute.

This ruling is based upon the principle that no animal renders the non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute except for an animal that has inherent sanctity, which means that even if it may not be sacrificed, it must still be left to graze in order to become blemished, after which it is sold, and the proceeds from the sale are used to purchase a fit offering.

notes.dh: ה"ג שאין לך דבר עושה תמורה אלא הרועה להסתאב
notes.he: כלומר שאין לך דבר שעושה תמורה אלא ההוא דקדוש קדושת הגוף שאם אינו ראוי להקריב אינו נמכר בלא מום אלא ירעה הילכך ר"ש סבירא ליה באשם ופסח הואיל ואין שמן חל עליהן בנקבה דנמכר שלא במום הילכך לא עביד תמורה אבל בעולה דאיכא שם עולה עלה בעוף סבירא ליה דתרעה ועבדא תמורה:
notes.en: This is the reading: “For nothing renders a substitute except what grazes until it becomes blemished.” That is, nothing renders a substitute except that which is consecrated with inherent sanctity, so that if it is not fit to be sacrificed it is not sold without a blemish but is left to graze. Therefore Rabbi Shimon holds that with a guilt offering and a Paschal offering, since their name does not take effect on a female, it is sold without a blemish, and so it does not render a substitute. But with a burnt offering, where there is burnt offering status for a bird, he holds that it grazes and renders a substitute.

notes.dh: שאין לך דבר שעושה תמורה אלא הרועה ומסתאב
notes.he: כלומר ההוא דקדוש קדושת הגוף שאם אינו ראוי להקריב אינו נמכר בלא מום אלא ירעה הילכך ר"ש סבירא ליה באשם ופסח הואיל ואין אשם ופסח חיילי בנקבה דנמכר בלא מום הילכך לא עבדי תמורה אבל בעולה דאיכא שם עולה בעוף ס"ל דתרעה ועבדא תמורה. לשון רש"י:
notes.en: For nothing renders a substitute except what grazes and becomes blemished: that is, that which is consecrated with inherent sanctity, so that if it is not fit to be sacrificed it is not sold without a blemish but grazes. Therefore Rabbi Shimon holds that with a guilt offering and a Paschal offering, since a guilt offering and a Paschal offering do not take effect on a female, it is sold without a blemish, and therefore they do not render a substitute. But with a burnt offering, where there is burnt offering status for a bird, he holds that it grazes and renders a substitute. [This is] Rashi’s wording.

messages.text: I do not agree with the statement of Rabbi Shimon with regard to the Paschal offering, that a non-sacred animal exchanged for a female which was designated for a Paschal offering does not become consecrated as a substitute. I disagree, since a leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed after Passover as a peace offering, and a peace offering is brought even from female animals.
messages.lead: With regard to this dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the first tanna:

notes.he: הילכך הואיל ושייכים שלמים בפסח ושלמים באין נקבה ואף על גב דהך לא קרבה נקבה אפילו שלמים לאחר הפסח כדאמרן לעיל (תמורה דף יט.) נשתיירה לאחר הפסח תרעה מיהו שם שלמים עלה הואיל והיא (שלמים) נקבה ונחתא לה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: Since a leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed as a peace offering: therefore, since peace offerings belong to the Paschal offering, and peace offerings come from females; and even though this female is not sacrificed even as a peace offering after Passover, as we said above (Temurah 19a) that if it remained after Passover it grazes, nevertheless the status of a peace offering is upon it, since it is female [and a peace offering may be female], and inherent sanctity descends upon it.

messages.text: Therefore, a female animal that was designated for a Paschal offering should be consecrated with inherent sanctity, as there is peace offering status for female animals. It should not be sold unless it has a blemish, and it should render a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute.

And let him also say: I do not agree with the statement of Rabbi Shimon with regard to a guilt offering, for the same reason that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi disagrees with regard to the Paschal offering, since a leftover guilt offering is sacrificed as a burnt offering, and a bird burnt offering is brought even from female animals. Therefore, a female animal designated as a guilt offering should be consecrated with inherent sanctity, and it should render a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute.
messages.quote: I do not agree with the statement of Rabbi Shimon with regard to the Paschal offering

notes.he: ואישתכח דהך נקבה דאשם עולה היא ותקדיש קדושת הגוף בעולה נקבה דהא מצינו עולת נקבה בעוף:
notes.en: Since a leftover guilt offering is sacrificed as a burnt offering: and it turns out that this female of the guilt offering is a burnt offering, so it should be consecrated with inherent sanctity as a female burnt offering, for we have found a female burnt offering among birds.

notes.dh: [אמר רבי אין אני רואה דבריו של ר' שמעון בפסח
notes.he: אלא ודאי עבדה תמורה הואיל ומותר הפסח קרב שלמים הא נקבה נמי דינה כמותר פסח וקרבה בדמיה שלמים וקדשה קדושת הגוף ועבדה תמורה. שהרי שלמים באין נקבה] וניתני נמי אין אני (נמי) רואה דבריו של ר' שמעון באשם אלא עבדה תמורה הואיל דאמרן לעיל במתניתין מותר אשם יקרב עולה והא נקבה נמי הויא כמותר אשם ותיקרב עולה דהא אשכחן עולה נקבה בעולת העוף ותיקדש קדושת הגוף ותיעביד תמורה:
notes.en: [Rabbi said: I do not agree with the statement of Rabbi Shimon with regard to the Paschal offering. Rather, it certainly renders a substitute, since a leftover Paschal offering is sacrificed as a peace offering; a female too has the law of a leftover Paschal offering, and with its money a peace offering is sacrificed; it is consecrated with inherent sanctity and renders a substitute, for peace offerings come from females.] And let him also teach: I do not agree with the statement of Rabbi Shimon with regard to a guilt offering; rather, it renders a substitute, since we said above in the mishna that a leftover guilt offering is sacrificed as a burnt offering. This female too is like a leftover guilt offering and should be sacrificed as a burnt offering, for we find a female burnt offering in the bird burnt offering; so it should be consecrated with inherent sanctity and render a substitute.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi holds in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who say: Leftover guilt offerings are used for communal gift offerings, i.e., they are sold and the money is used to purchase communal gift offerings, and a substitute cannot be designated for a communal offering.

notes.he: ואי נמי הויא עולה הואיל ולעולת צבור קיימא לא עבדה תמורה:
notes.en: For communal gift offerings: and even if it is a burnt offering, since it stands to become a communal burnt offering, it does not render a substitute.

notes.dh: רבי סבר כרבנן דאמרי מותרות לנדבת צבור אזלי ואין תמורה בצבור
notes.he: ותימה מאי קאמר דלעיל משמע דתולה תמורה ברעייה והכא משמע דתולה רעייה בתמורה לימא דלירעו ויעשה תמורה ונראה דה"פ כיון דלנדבת צבור אזלי ואין תמורה בצבור אין לומר דליהני ליה למפריש נקבה לאשם להיות קדוש קדושת הגוף משום דמותר אשם קרב עולה כיון דאין דינם שוה (לתמורה דאשם עושה תמורה) ואין מותר אשם עושה תמורה דלנדבת צבור אזיל דלא עביד תמורה ולא דמי למפריש נקבה לפסח דמותר פסח הוי לשלמים שעושים תמורה כמו הפסח עצמו הילכך דין הוא שיחול קדושת הגוף על נקבה שהפרישה לפסח דכך לי הפרישה לפסח כאילו הפרישו למותר פסח דהיינו שלמים דשניהן עושין תמורה:
notes.en: Rabbi holds in accordance with the Rabbis, who say that leftovers go to communal gift offerings, and there is no substitute for a communal offering: This is puzzling: what is he saying? Above it implies that he makes substitution depend on grazing, and here it implies that he makes grazing depend on substitution. Let him say that they graze and render a substitute! It seems that this is the explanation: since they go to communal gift offerings, and there is no substitute for a communal offering, one cannot say that it helps one who designates a female for a guilt offering to be consecrated with inherent sanctity because a leftover guilt offering is sacrificed as a burnt offering. For their law is not the same: a guilt offering renders a substitute, and a leftover guilt offering does not, since it goes to communal gift offerings, which do not render a substitute. It is not like one who designates a female for a Paschal offering, for a leftover Paschal offering becomes a peace offering, which renders a substitute just as the Paschal offering itself does. Therefore it is right that inherent sanctity should take effect on a female he designated for a Paschal offering, for it is all the same whether he designated it for a Paschal offering or for a leftover Paschal offering, that is, a peace offering, since both render a substitute.

notes.he: מותרות דקרבי עולה:
notes.en: Rabbi holds: [that] the leftovers, which are sacrificed as burnt offerings, [go to communal gift offerings].

notes.he: לעולת צבור ואין תמורה בצבור:
notes.en: They go to communal gift offerings: to communal burnt offerings, and there is no substitute for a communal offering.

messages.text: It might enter your mind to say that this is the reason for the ruling of Rabbi Shimon with regard to one who designates a female animal for his burnt offering: One renders a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute due to that reason, that it has burnt offering status because of the case of a bird burnt offering, which may be brought as a female.
messages.quote: if he consecrates a female animal for his burnt offering, it renders the non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute

notes.he: גבי עני בעולת העוף ולפי הא דס"ד השתא רוצה לומר מפריש נקבה לעולתו כגון מצורע עשיר שצריך להביא עולת בהמה זכר ומש"ה קאמר דעושין תמורה בהפריש נקבה לעולתו משום דהאי חיובא דמחויב שייך בנקבה אם היה עני שמפריש עולת העוף דבאה נקבה דאין תמות וזכרות בעוף ומש"ה נקט גבי עני כגון עני מצורע דבהאי חיובא דקמחייב איכא נקבה בעולה:
notes.en: Since it has burnt offering status: with regard to a poor man, in the bird burnt offering. As it now enters your mind, [the case] means one who designates a female for his burnt offering, for example a wealthy leper who must bring a male animal as a burnt offering. That is why it says that he renders a substitute when he designated a female for his burnt offering: because this very obligation he owes applies to a female if he were poor, for he would designate a bird burnt offering, which may be female, since unblemished status and maleness do not apply to birds. That is why it took the case of a poor man, such as a poor leper: in this very obligation that he owes there is a female burnt offering.

messages.text: But if that is so, in the case of a High Priest who designated a female cow instead of his male bull that he is obligated to bring as a sin offering on Yom Kippur, it should be sanctified with regard to rendering a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute. Here too, the status of a sin offering is upon it, as the red heifer of purification is similar to a sin offering and is female.

notes.he: פר יום הכפורים דחטאת דהא איכא שם חטאת עלה דהא אשכחנא פרה אדומה דמיקריא חטאת (חולין דף יא.):
notes.en: For his bull: the bull of Yom Kippur, which is a sin offering; for there is sin offering status upon it, since we find the red heifer, which is called a sin offering (Ḥullin 11a).

notes.he: תימה לפי מה דפירשתי דאיכא למצוא נקבה בעולה בהאי חיובא גופיה דקמחייב והכא לא שייך למימר הכי ועוד אמאי נקט פרת חטאת רוב חטאת המזבח נקבה אתיא וי"ל דפריך מכ"ש דהא אפילו מפריש נקבה לעולה דהיא גופה לא חזיא לעולה אפילו הכי קאמר דעושה תמורה משום דאיכא שם עולה עליה בעולת העוף כ"ש מפריש פרה לפרו דהיא גופה חזיא לפרת חטאת אם היא אדומה דאית לן למימר דתיקדוש:
notes.en: Since there is the heifer of purification [parat ḥatat]: This is puzzling according to what I explained, that a female burnt offering can be found within the very obligation he owes, whereas here one cannot say so. Furthermore, why did it take the heifer of purification? Most sin offerings of the altar come as females! One can say that he objects a fortiori: even one who designates a female for a burnt offering, which itself is not fit for a burnt offering, [Rabbi Shimon] nevertheless says renders a substitute because it has burnt offering status from the bird burnt offering. All the more so one who designates a cow for his bull, since the cow itself is fit to be a heifer of purification if it is red, so we should say that it is consecrated.

notes.he: שלו שמביא ביוה"כ לחטאתו:
notes.en: Who designated a female cow for his bull: his own bull, which he brings on Yom Kippur as his sin offering.

notes.he: שהרי מצינו פרת חטאת פרה אדומה דנקבה היא וקרויה חטאת:
notes.en: It should be consecrated and render a substitute: for we have found the heifer of purification, the red heifer, which is female and is called a sin offering.

messages.text: The red heifer is not consecrated with inherent sanctity, as it is not sacrificed upon the altar; rather, it is consecrated for Temple maintenance, and items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not render a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for them a substitute.

notes.he: ולא קרבה למזבח ולהכי קרי ליה בדק הבית כלומר דדין בדק הבית אית לה:
notes.en: It is consecrated for Temple maintenance: it is not sacrificed on the altar, and that is why he calls it Temple maintenance; that is, it has the law of Temple maintenance.

notes.he: מיהא לא איריא דפרת חטאת קדשי בדק הבית היא ולית בהו תמורה דלא קדשי קדושת הגוף וליכא לאקשויי מיהא:
notes.en: In any case this is no proof, for the heifer of purification is consecrated for Temple maintenance, and such items have no substitute, since they are not consecrated with inherent sanctity; so there is no difficulty from it.

messages.text: According to Rabbi Shimon, if an individual, who is obligated to bring a female animal as a sin offering, designated a male goat instead of his female goat, it should be sanctified with inherent sanctity with regard to rendering a substitute, as it has sin offering status, due to the case of the male goat brought as a sin offering by the king.

notes.dh: יחיד שהפריש שעיר לשעירתו תיקדוש דהא איכא שעיר נשיא
notes.he: וה"ה דהוה מצי למיפרך מברייתא גופא דלעיל דאשם בן שנה והביאו בן שתים דקאמר ר' שמעון כל עצמן אינן קדושין ואמאי הא חזי לאשם מעילות וגזילות והאי שינויא דקמשני שייך נמי עלה:
notes.en: An individual who designated a male goat for his female goat, it should be consecrated, since there is the king’s goat: He could equally have objected from the baraita itself above, about a guilt offering that must be one year old and he brought one two years old, where Rabbi Shimon says that they are not consecrated at all. But why not? It is fit for the guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property and for robbery! And the answer given here applies to it as well.

messages.text: Alternatively, if a king, who is obligated to bring a male animal as a sin offering, designated a female goat instead of his male goat, it should be sanctified with inherent sanctity with regard to rendering a substitute, since here too it has sin offering status, as an individual designates a female goat as a sin offering. Therefore, Rabbi Shimon should have stated that these animals render non-sacred animals exchanged for them consecrated as substitutes.

Neither a female goat brought as a sin offering by a king nor a male goat brought as a sin offering by an individual are considered to have sin offering status. The reason is that these, the king and an individual, are two distinct bodies, and the status of an offering can be conferred only when such an offering is brought by people of the same status.

notes.he: יחיד ונשיא ומיהו בהאי גופא דיחיד לא משכחת שעיר לחטאת ובהאי גופא דנשיא לא משכחת לה שעירה אבל עולה נקבה בהאי גופא משכחת לה דאי בעי מפקר לנכסיה והוי עני וחזיא ליה עולת העוף:
notes.en: These are two bodies: an individual and a king [nasi]. In the body of an individual you do not find a male goat as a sin offering, and in the body of a king you do not find a female goat. But a female burnt offering you do find in this same body: if he wishes he can renounce ownership of his property and become poor, and a bird burnt offering is fit for him.

notes.he: פירש"י יחיד ונשיא ומיהו בהאי גופא דיחיד לא משכחת שעיר חטאת ובהאי גופא דנשיא לא משכחת שעירה אבל עולה נקבה בהאי גופא משכחת לה דאי בעי מפקר לנכסיה והוי עני וחזי ליה עולת העוף עכ"ל ול"נ דמאי קפריך בסמוך אי הכי הא נמי לא עולת העוף קמייתי מ"מ לא דמו דהיא גופה חזי לעולת נקבה אי מפקר נכסיה לכ"נ לפרש הני תרי גופי נינהו דהאי יחיד לא חזי להיות נשיא בעוד הנשיא חי ונשיא לא חזי להיות לו דין יחיד אבל עני ועשיר כחד גופא דמו העשיר ראוי להיות עני ועני ראוי להיות עשיר והשתא פריך שפיר אי הכי דאמר הא לא חטא ולא איחייב בשעיר אע"ג דגופו ראוי להיות נשיא כיון דבההיא שעתא דחטא לא איחייב בשעיר לאו כגוף אחד קרינא ביה הכי נמי בההיא שעתא דחטא לא איחייב בעולת העוף ולא מצי פטר נפשיה בה:
notes.en: These are two bodies: Rashi explained: an individual and a king; in the body of an individual you do not find a male goat as a sin offering, and in the body of a king you do not find a female goat, but a female burnt offering you do find in this same body, since if he wishes he can renounce his property and become poor, and a bird burnt offering is fit for him. End of his words. But this does not seem right to me, for what does it object shortly after, “If so, here too he does not bring a bird burnt offering”? Either way the cases are not alike, since he himself is fit for a female burnt offering if he renounces his property. Therefore it seems to me to explain “these are two bodies” thus: this individual is not fit to become king while the king is alive, and the king is not fit to have the status of an individual; but poor and rich are like one body, for the rich man is fit to become poor and the poor man fit to become rich. Now the objection is sound: if so, as he said, “He did not sin [as king] and was not obligated to bring a male goat,” even though his body was fit to become king, since at the time he sinned he was not obligated to bring a male goat, it is not called one body; so too here, at the time he sinned he was not obligated to bring a bird burnt offering, and he cannot discharge his obligation with it.

notes.dh: יחיד שמביא לחטאתו כשבה או שעירה והפריש שעיר
notes.he: לשום שעירתו תיקדוש קדושת הגוף ותעביד תמורה דהא איכא שם חטאת עליו שהרי נשיא מביא שעיר לחטאתו. לא דמי להכא משום הכי לא קדיש דתרי גופי נינהו יחיד ונשיא דמאי דמייתי האי לא מייתי האי אבל הכא גבי יחיד מפריש נקבה לעולתו משום הכי קדשה שהרי הוא עצמו אם הוא עני או אם ירצה להפקיר נכסיו להיות עני יכול להביא עולת העוף נקבה:
notes.en: An individual, who brings a ewe or a female goat as his sin offering, and designated a male goat for his female goat: it should be consecrated with inherent sanctity and render a substitute, since sin offering status is upon it, for a king brings a male goat as his sin offering. [The answer:] It is not like the case here, and that is why it is not consecrated: an individual and a king are two bodies, and what this one brings, that one does not bring. But here, with an individual who designates a female for his burnt offering, it is consecrated, for he himself, if he is poor, or if he wishes to renounce his property and become poor, can bring a female bird burnt offering.

messages.text: If so, then in a case where an individual sinned and is obligated to bring a female goat as a sin offering prior to being appointed as king, and he did not designate an animal as his offering before his appointment, if he designates a male goat instead of his female goat following his appointment, it should be sanctified with inherent sanctity with regard to substitution. In this situation, it should have sin offering status, as, if he sinned now, he is obligated to bring a male goat.
messages.quote: these, the king and an individual, are two distinct bodies

notes.he: שם חטאת עליה בהאי גופא דאילו חטא השתא בר איתויי שעיר הוא:
notes.en: He sinned before he was appointed: [the questioner reasons that] there is sin offering status upon it in this same body, since if he sinned now he would be obligated to bring a male goat.

notes.he: להיות נשיא אם הפריש שעיר לשום שעירתו שהוא חייב להביא שהוא עדיין הדיוט ניקדוש דהא אילו חטא השתא לאחר שנתמנה היה צריך להביא שעיר דהכא גוף אחד הוא הדיוט ונשיא:
notes.en: They sinned before they were appointed as king: if he designated a male goat for the female goat that he is obligated to bring, since he was still a commoner, it should be consecrated, for if he sinned now, after he was appointed, he would need to bring a male goat; here the commoner and the king are one body.

messages.text: This is not correct, as he did not sin when he was a king, and therefore was not actually obligated to bring a male goat, but a female goat.

notes.he: התם משום הכי לא מייתי שעיר אע"ג דגוף אחד הוא דהא לא חטא כשהוא נשיא ולא איחייב בשעיר הילכך אי מייתי שעיר כשהוא הדיוט לא קדיש:
notes.en: Even so, it is not alike. There, the reason he does not bring a male goat, even though he is one body, is that he did not sin when he was king and was not obligated to bring a male goat; therefore if he brings a male goat [for a sin committed] when he was a commoner, it is not consecrated.

messages.text: If so, that the individual’s appointment as king does not give sin offering status to the male goat designated as a sin offering for a sin committed prior to his appointment, here too, one should say that a female animal designated for a burnt offering does not have burnt offering status, as the person is not a poor leper, and therefore he does not bring a bird burnt offering. Why, then, does Rabbi Shimon maintain that such an animal renders a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute?
messages.quote: he did not sin when he was a king, and therefore was not actually obligated

notes.he: אי הוה מחויב עולה לא הוה מייתי עולת העוף דעשיר הוא וא"נ עני הוא עולת נדבה לא קרבה בדלות אי לא פריש בהדיא עוף:
notes.en: He does not bring a bird burnt offering [Rashi’s heading adds, in parentheses, “he is wealthy”]: if he were obligated to bring a burnt offering he would not bring a bird burnt offering, since he is wealthy. And even if he is poor, a voluntary burnt offering is not brought in the form of poverty unless he explicitly specified a bird.

notes.he: גבי מפריש נקבה לעולתו לא ליקדיש דעשיר הוא מי שמפריש בהמה [לעולה ולא בר אייתוי עולת העוף נקבה הוא אלא היינו טעמא דר' שמעון גבי עולה דסבר דעשיר נמי מצי מייתי עולת העוף כר' אלעזר בן עזריה]:
notes.en: If so, here too: with one who designates a female for his burnt offering, it should not be consecrated, for one who designates an animal [for a burnt offering] is wealthy and cannot bring a female bird burnt offering. [Rather, this is Rabbi Shimon’s reason with regard to a burnt offering: he holds that a wealthy man too can bring a bird burnt offering, in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.]

messages.text: The baraita is not referring to an obligatory burnt offering but rather to a voluntary burnt offering, and Rabbi Shimon holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, who says that anyone, even a wealthy man, can bring a bird if he vows to bring a burnt offering.

notes.dh: רבי שמעון סבר לה כרבי אלעזר בן עזריה
notes.he: דאפילו גבי נדבה דעשיר סתם חזיא עולת העוף:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: that even for an unspecified gift offering of a wealthy man, a bird burnt offering is fit.

notes.dh: רבי שמעון סבר כר"א בן עזריה כו'
notes.he: יביא תור או בני יונה פירוש וכיון דמצי פטר נפשיה בעוף אפילו לאחר הפרשת בהמה כדאי' פ' מרובה (ב"ק דף עח:) וא"כ דחי שפיר בעולת נקבה וצ"ל דמיירי השתא הא דר"ש דמפריש נקבה לעולתו באומר הרי עלי עולה דמצי פטר נפשיה בעולת העוף נקבה אפילו לאחר הפרשת בהמה כדאי' פ' מרובה (גם זה שם):
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya etc.: he brings a turtledove or pigeons. That is, since he can discharge his obligation with a bird even after designating an animal, as is stated in chapter Merubba (Bava Kamma 78b), it rejects [the objection] well with regard to a female burnt offering. And one must say that Rabbi Shimon’s case of one who designates a female for his burnt offering is now dealing with one who says, “It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering,” who can discharge his obligation with a female bird burnt offering even after designating an animal, as is stated in chapter Merubba (also there).

messages.text: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering, without specifying which animal, brings a lamb, which is the smallest animal that a wealthy man can bring as a burnt offering.
He may even bring a dove or pigeons as a bird burnt offering.

messages.caption: Can a status found in another offering give inherent sanctity? The cases the Gemara tests against Rabbi Shimon, and its answers.

messages.text: In the case of one who consecrates all his possessions without specifying for what purpose, and among them there is an animal that is suitable to be sacrificed on the altar, or multiple such animals that are males and females, what should be done with them?
messages.lead: § The Gemara continues to discuss Rabbi Shimon’s opinion in the baraita: We learned in a mishna elsewhere (Shekalim 4:7):

messages.text: Since he did not specify otherwise, everything is consecrated for Temple maintenance. Therefore, any males should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as burnt offerings. And any females, as they cannot be brought as burnt offerings, should be sold for the needs of peace offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as such. And their monetary value that is received from their sale is allocated with the rest of his property for Temple maintenance.

notes.dh: ודמיהם יפלו עם שאר נכסים לבדק הבית
notes.he: דסבר ר"א סתם הקדשות לבדק הבית ואפילו בהמה ומיהו מידי דחזי למזבח אינו יוצא מידי מזבח לעולם. ור' יהושע סבר לא שביק איניש קדושת מזבח ומקדיש לבדק הבית מידי דחזי למזבח הילכך מסתמא למזבח אקדשינהו והן עצמן יקרבו עולות:
notes.en: And their monetary value is allocated with the rest of the property for Temple maintenance: for Rabbi Eliezer holds that unspecified consecrations are for Temple maintenance, even an animal; yet something fit for the altar never leaves the altar’s claim. And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that a person does not forgo the sanctity of the altar and consecrate for Temple maintenance something that is fit for the altar; therefore, presumably he consecrated them for the altar, and they themselves are sacrificed as burnt offerings.

notes.dh: ימכרו לצרכי עולה ויפלו דמיהן עם שאר נכסים לבדק הבית
notes.he: דקסבר רבי אליעזר סתם הקדש לבדק הבית והוי כמתפיס תמימים לבדק הבית דאינו יוצא מידי מזבח לעולם:
notes.en: They are sold for the needs of burnt offerings, and their monetary value is allocated with the rest of the property for Temple maintenance: for Rabbi Eliezer holds that unspecified consecration is for Temple maintenance, and it is like one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, which never leave the altar’s claim.

messages.text: Although he did not specify for what purpose he consecrated his possessions, it may be assumed that he intended the animals to be consecrated as burnt offerings. Therefore, any males should themselves be sacrificed as burnt offerings, and any females, since they cannot be brought as burnt offerings, should be sold for the needs of peace offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as such, and their monetary value that is received from their sale should be used to purchase and bring burnt offerings. And according to both opinions, the rest of the property, which is not suitable for sacrificial use, is allocated for Temple maintenance.

notes.dh: ונקבות ימכרו כו' ויביאו בדמיהן עולות
notes.he: דסתמייהו לעולה אקדשינהו:
notes.en: And the females are sold etc., and he brings burnt offerings with their money: for when he did not specify, he consecrated them as a burnt offering.

notes.dh: ורבי יהושע אמר זכרים עצמן יקרבו עולה
notes.he: דקסבר לא שביק אינש קדשי מזבח ואקדיש לקדשי בדק הבית מידי דחזי לקדשי מזבח וסתמא דעתו לעולה דכולה כליל לשם:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehoshua says the males themselves are sacrificed as burnt offerings: for he holds that a person does not forgo sacrifices of the altar and consecrate for Temple maintenance something that is fit for sacrifices of the altar, and his unspecified intention is for a burnt offering, which is burned entirely to the Name.

notes.he: ר' יהושע אמר זכרים עצמן יקרבו עולות [ונקבות ימכרו לצרכי שלמים ויביא בדמיהן עולות כדמפרש טעמיה בפרק בתרא יש בקדשי מזבח דלא שביק איניש קדשי מזבח דבר הראוי למזבח כולו לאשים ומקדשינהו לבדק הבית ועוד דסבר דאדם חולק את נדרו דבהמה לקדשי מזבח ושאר נכסים לקדשי בדק הבית:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: The males themselves are sacrificed as burnt offerings, [and the females are sold for the needs of peace offerings and he brings burnt offerings with their money. His reason is explained in the last chapter, Yesh BeKodshei Mizbe’aḥ: a person does not forgo sacrifices of the altar, something fit for the altar to be wholly for the fires, and consecrate them for Temple maintenance. Furthermore, he holds that a person divides his vow: the animals for sacrifices of the altar and the rest of the property for Temple maintenance.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yoḥanan According to the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua, who said that any males should themselves be sacrificed as burnt offerings, as that was the intention of the one who consecrated them, how can the buyers sacrifice the females as peace offerings? Their status stems from deferred sanctity, as they were consecrated to be burnt offerings, and a female that was designated as a burnt offering is not sacrificed upon the altar, but instead is left to graze until it becomes blemished and is then sold.
messages.quote: males should themselves be sacrificed as burnt offerings

notes.he: דכיון דזכרים קרבו עולות ודמי השלמים עולות מכלל דסבירא ליה דסתמא לעולה אקדשינהו והוה ליה מפריש נקבה לעולה והיכי יקרב שלמים הא בעי לרעות כדקתני מתני' (לעיל תמורה יח:) המפריש נקבה לעולה תרעה:
notes.en: Their status stems from deferred sanctity: since the males are sacrificed as burnt offerings and the money of the peace offerings goes for burnt offerings, it follows that he holds that, unspecified, he consecrated them as a burnt offering. It is then a case of one who designates a female for a burnt offering, so how can it be sacrificed as a peace offering? It needs to graze, as our mishna teaches (above, Temurah 18b): One who designates a female for a burnt offering, it grazes.

notes.he: מדקאמר זכרים עצמן יקרבו עולות] מכלל דכל בהמות אקדשינהו לשום עולות ונקבה לא מצי קרבו עולות והיכי מצי למיקרב שלמים הני שלמים מכח קדושה דחויה אתיאן דלשום עולות כולהו אקדישינהו ולא חזי לעולה:
notes.en: How can the females be sacrificed as peace offerings? From his saying that the males themselves are sacrificed as burnt offerings,] it follows that he consecrated all the animals as burnt offerings, and a female cannot be sacrificed as a burnt offering; so how can it be sacrificed as a peace offering? These peace offerings come from deferred sanctity, since he consecrated them all as burnt offerings and it is not fit for a burnt offering.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yoḥanan From the fact that Rabbi Yehoshua said that any males should themselves be sacrificed as burnt offerings, is this to say that he consecrated them with inherent sanctity? If so, why are the females sold for the needs of peace offerings? Since they were consecrated as burnt offerings, it is required that they be left to graze until they become blemished.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites another version of this statement:

notes.he: ל"א למימרא דקדושת הגוף לשום עולה לאשים אקדישינון לכולהו:
notes.en: Another version: Is this to say [that he consecrated them with] inherent sanctity? He consecrated all of them as a burnt offering, for the fires.

notes.he: נקבות דמכח קדושה דחויה אתיין:
notes.en: But they require grazing: the females, since they come from deferred sanctity.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehoshua holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who said with regard to anything that is not fit to be sacrificed itself upon the altar that inherent sanctity does not descend upon it. As we learned in the mishna that Rabbi Shimon says: If one designated a female for a guilt offering, for which one must bring a male, it may be sold without a blemish, and a guilt offering is purchased with the money received for its sale. And we say that the reason of Rabbi Shimon is that as a female animal is not fit to be sacrificed as a guilt offering, inherent sanctity does not descend upon it.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba:

notes.he: ר' יהושע סבר לה כר' שמעון דאמר תימכר שלא במום בכל מידי דלא חזי לגופיה להקרבה לא נחתא לה קדושת הגוף לשם ההוא זבח הילכך לא בעי רעייה אלא (ימכרו לצרכי) [קרבי] שלמים:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who said “it is sold without a blemish”: anything that is not itself fit for sacrifice, inherent sanctity for that offering does not descend upon it. Therefore it does not require grazing, but is sacrificed as a peace offering.

messages.text: You can say that Rabbi Shimon expressed his opinion specifically with regard to one who consecrates a female for a guilt offering,
messages.lead: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba objected to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
messages.quote: Rabbi Yehoshua holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon

notes.he: לא נחתא ליה קדושת הגוף גבי נקבה לאשם:
notes.en: Say that Rabbi Shimon said: that inherent sanctity does not descend upon it, with regard to a female for a guilt offering.

messages.text: where there is no guilt offering status for an animal that is the same sex as its mother, as a female guilt offering is never brought. But with regard to one who designates a female animal as a burnt offering, where there is burnt offering status for a bird that is the same sex as its mother, even Rabbi Shimon concedes that it has inherent sanctity, and therefore it should not be sold for the needs of a peace offering.

notes.he: דלא אשכחן נקבה:
notes.en: Where there is no guilt offering status for its mother: for we have not found a female [guilt offering].

notes.he: עליה בנקבה אבל גבי נקבה לעולה דאיכא שם עולה בנקבה אפילו ר' שמעון מודי דקדשה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: Where there is no guilt offering status: upon it, for a female. But with a female for a burnt offering, where there is burnt offering status for a female, even Rabbi Shimon concedes that it is consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: In addition, another objection can be raised against the explanation of Rabbi Yoḥanan, as we have heard that Rabbi Shimon maintains that one who designates a female animal as a burnt offering renders a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute. This indicates that it does have inherent sanctity with regard to this issue. Therefore, the question remains: How can the buyers sacrifice the females as peace offerings, when their status stems from deferred sanctity?

notes.he: אלמא נחתא לה קדושת הגוף לרעות. לשון ירושלמי נקבות היכי קרבי שלמים הא קדוש גופייהו לעולה כלומר ובעו רעייה דהא אמרינן (ב"ק דף עח:) אי בעי פטר נפשיה בעולת העוף כלומר בעולת נקבה:
notes.en: Renders a substitute: evidently inherent sanctity descends upon it, so that it must graze. A Jerusalem version reads: How can the females be sacrificed as peace offerings? Their bodies are consecrated as a burnt offering; that is, they need to graze, for we say (Bava Kamma 78b) that if he wishes he can discharge his obligation with a bird burnt offering, that is, with a female burnt offering.

notes.he: דקדשה לגופה דהא אוקימנא לר"ש לעיל דסבירא ליה כר' אלעזר בן עזריה:
notes.en: In addition, Rabbi Shimon said: that it is consecrated in its body, for we established above that Rabbi Shimon holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

notes.he: דאמר אף לעולתו עושה תמורה אלמא דקדש קדושת הגוף והיכי מצי קרבי שלמים. ר' יהושע סבר לה כאידך תנא אליבא דר' שמעון כו' דאמר אף לעולתו אין עושה תמורה:
notes.en: In addition, we have heard: that he said that for his burnt offering it renders a substitute; evidently it is consecrated with inherent sanctity, so how can they be sacrificed as peace offerings? Rabbi Yehoshua holds in accordance with the other tanna’s view of Rabbi Shimon etc., who said that even for his burnt offering it does not render a substitute.

messages.text: I meant that Rabbi Yehoshua holds in accordance with the interpretation of the other tanna with regard to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon. As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.lead: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba in response:

messages.text: Even one who consecrates a female as his burnt offering does not render a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it a substitute.

Even though there is burnt offering status for female birds, a female animal consecrated as a burnt offering does not have inherent sanctity. Therefore, it is sold and sacrificed as a peace offering, and its status is not considered to stem from deferred sanctity.
Mishna

With regard to the substitute of a guilt offering, the offspring of that substitute, their offspring and the offspring of their offspring, until the end of all time, they are all left to graze until they become unfit, and then they are sold, and the money received for the sale is allocated for communal gift offerings.

notes.he: בין זכר בין נקבה תרעה דהילכתא גמירי לה (לעיל תמורה דף יח.) כל שבחטאת מתה באשם תרעה:
notes.en: Mishna: The substitute of a guilt offering, whether male or female, grazes, for it is learned as a halakha [transmitted from Sinai] (above, Temurah 18a): whatever is left to die in the case of a sin offering is left to graze in the case of a guilt offering.

notes.he: כגון אם המיר (הפריש) נקבה לאשמו וילדה:
notes.en: The offspring of a substitute: for example, if he exchanged [another reading: designated] a female for his guilt offering, and it gave birth.

notes.he: אפילו זכר ולדן כשהתמורה נקבה:
notes.en: The substitute of a guilt offering: even a male; their offspring: when the substitute is female.

notes.he: או ולד ולדן ירעו דקי"ל כל שבחטאת מתה באשם רועה ותמורת חטאת מתה:
notes.en: Or the offspring of their offspring, they graze: for we hold that whatever is left to die in the case of a sin offering is left to graze in the case of a guilt offering, and the substitute of a sin offering is left to die.

notes.he: דמותר אשם דמיו קרב עולה:
notes.en: And their money is allocated for communal gift offerings: since the money of a leftover guilt offering is sacrificed as a burnt offering.

messages.text: These animals are not left to graze; rather they are left to die.

notes.he: כדמפרש בגמ' דגזר לאחר כפרה אטו לפני כפרה:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: They are left to die: as the Gemara explains, that he decreed after atonement on account of before atonement.

messages.text: Communal gift offerings are not purchased with the money from the sale; rather, the owner should bring an individual burnt offering with the money received for its sale.

notes.he: ר' אלעזר אומר יביא בדמיהן עולה לנדבת יחיד:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar says: He brings a burnt offering with their money, as an individual’s gift offering.

messages.text: A guilt offering whose owner died, and a guilt offering that was lost and its owner gained atonement with another animal, graze until they become unfit, and then they are sold, and the money received for the sale is allocated for communal gift offerings.
messages.lead: These tanna’im similarly disagree about the following case:

notes.dh: אשם שמתו בעליו או שנתכפרו בעליו
notes.he: באשם אחר ונשתייר ראשון ירעה כו':
notes.en: A guilt offering whose owner died, or whose owner achieved atonement: with another guilt offering, and the first remained: it grazes etc.

messages.text: These animals are left to die.
The owner must bring an individual burnt offering with the money received for its sale.

notes.he: דמותרות לנדבת יחיד אזלי:
notes.en: He brings a burnt offering: for the leftovers go to an individual’s gift offering.

messages.text: But even according to the Rabbis, isn’t a gift offering also a burnt offering? And what then is the difference between the statement of Rabbi Elazar and the statement of the Rabbis?

notes.he: בניחותא אלא פרושי מפרש ואזיל מאי בינייהו:
notes.en: But isn’t a gift offering also a burnt offering: this is said as a statement [not a challenge]; rather, it goes on to explain what the difference between them is.

messages.text: Rather, the Rabbis are referring to a communal burnt offering and Rabbi Elazar is referring to an individual burnt offering, and there are several differences between these two offerings: When the animal comes as an individual burnt offering, the owner places his hands upon it and brings the accompanying meal offering and libations, and its libations come from his own property. If the owner of the animal was a priest, the right to perform its Temple service and the right to its hide are his.

notes.he: שהיא מוטלת על היחיד להקריבה סומך עליה כו':
notes.en: When it comes as an obligation [Rashi’s text reads “as an obligation” where ours reads “as a burnt offering”]: that it is incumbent on the individual to sacrifice it, he places his hands on it etc.

notes.he: אותו שהפריש האשם וכפר באחר וניתק הראשון לרעייה:
notes.en: And if he was a priest: the one who designated the guilt offering, achieved atonement with another, and the first was consigned to grazing.

notes.he: של עולה הבאה מן המותר:
notes.en: Its service and its hide: of the burnt offering that comes from the leftover.

notes.he: שהוא [עצמו] מקריבה ונוטל את העור ואפילו אינו מאותו משמר המשמרת באותה שבת דהכי תניא מנין לכהן שבא ומקריב קרבנותיו בכל עת ובכל שעה שירצה ת"ל ובא בכל אות נפשו ושרת בב"ק בשילהי הגוזל קמא (בבא קמא דף קט:):
notes.en: Are his: he himself sacrifices it and takes the hide, even if he is not of the priestly watch serving that week. For so it is taught: From where is it derived that a priest may come and sacrifice his offerings at any time and at any hour he wishes? The verse states: “And he comes with all the desire of his soul… and he shall minister” (Deuteronomy 18:6–7); in Bava Kamma, at the end of the first chapter HaGozel (Bava Kamma 109b).

notes.dh: אם היה כהן עבודתה ועורה שלו
notes.he: פירוש אם היה כהן זה שהמותר שלו הוא עצמו מקריבה והעור שלו ואפילו אינו מאותו משמר המשמרת באותה שבת דהכי תניא מנין לכהן שבא ומקריב קרבנותיו בכל עת ובכל שעה שירצה ת"ל ובא בכל אות נפשו ושרת בב"ק בשילהי הגוזל קמא (בבא קמא דף קט:) לשון רש"י:
notes.en: If he was a priest, its service and its hide are his: that is, if this priest to whom the leftover belongs, he himself sacrifices it and the hide is his, even if he is not of the priestly watch serving that week. For so it is taught: From where is it derived that a priest may come and sacrifice his offerings at any time and at any hour he wishes? The verse states: “And he comes with all the desire of his soul… and he shall minister”; in Bava Kamma, at the end of the first chapter HaGozel (Bava Kamma 109b). [This is] Rashi’s wording.

messages.text: And when it is a communal gift offering, the owner of the animal that was sold does not place his hands upon it, as there is no placing of hands for communal offerings, and he does not bring its libations; rather, its libations are brought from the property of the community. Furthermore, although the owner of the animal that was sold is a priest, the right to perform its Temple service and the right to its hide are divided among the members of the priestly watch serving in the Temple that week.

notes.he: דקרבן צבור אין בו סמיכה חוץ מפר העלם דבר של צבור ושעיר המשתלח דגמירי שתי סמיכות בצבור במנחות בפרק שתי מדות (מנחות דף צב.):
notes.en: And he does not place his hands on it: for a communal offering has no placing of hands, except the bull for an unwitting communal sin and the scapegoat, since we have a tradition of two placings of hands in a community; in Menaḥot, chapter Shetei Middot (Menaḥot 92a).

notes.he: כלומר ואפילו הוא כהן עבודתה ועורה של אנשי משמר שהרי של צבור היא ואין כהן של משמר אחר רשאי להקריב דכתיב לבד ממכריו על האבות מה מסרו אבות זה לזה אני בשבתי ואתם בשבתכם:
notes.en: And although he is a priest: that is, even if he is a priest, its service and its hide belong to the men of the priestly watch, since it is communal, and a priest of another watch may not sacrifice it, as it is written: “Beside that which is sold according to the fathers’ houses” (Deuteronomy 18:8): what did the fathers hand over to one another? I in my week and you in your week.

messages.caption: The mishna’s three views on the substitute of a guilt offering and on a guilt offering whose owner died or achieved atonement, and how an individual’s burnt offering differs from a communal gift offering.

messages.text: Gemara
The mishna teaches that Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages disagreed about two cases, the substitute of a guilt offering and the halakha of a guilt offering whose owner died. Both disputes are necessary.

notes.he: לאיפלוגי בתרתי ר' אליעזר ורבנן:
notes.en: Gemara: And it is necessary: for Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis to disagree about two cases.

notes.he: למיפלג בתרוייהו בפי' בתמורת אשם ובאשם שמתו בעלים:
notes.en: And it is necessary: for them to disagree explicitly in both, in the substitute of a guilt offering and in a guilt offering whose owner died.

messages.text: As, had the tanna taught us the dispute only in the case of the guilt offering where the owner achieved atonement through another animal, I might have said that perhaps it is in this case alone that Rabbi Eliezer says that the animals are left to die. This would be because he holds that there is a rabbinic decree concerning what to do with a guilt offering following the owner having achieved atonement, due to the case of a guilt offering before the owner achieved atonement.

notes.he: שכיפרו בעליו בההוא קאמר רבי אליעזר ימות משום דגזר אחר כפרה שנתכפר בראשון אי אמרת יביא בדמי המותר עולה אתי למימר נמי קודם כפרה אם נפל בו מום (אחר) אתי לאתויי בדמיו עולה וקעביד איסורא דכל זמן שלא נתכפר קיימי דמיה לאשם:
notes.en: As, had it taught us a guilt offering whose owner achieved atonement: in that case Rabbi Eliezer says it dies, because he decreed after atonement, when he achieved atonement with the first [i.e., with another animal]. If you say he brings a burnt offering with the money of the leftover, people would come to say so before atonement too: if a blemish befell it, they would come to bring a burnt offering with its money, and he would commit a prohibition, for as long as he has not achieved atonement its money stands for a guilt offering.

notes.he: בחדא באשם שמתו בעלים או שנתכפרו בהא קאמר ר' אליעזר ימותו משום דגזר לאחר כפרה אטו לפני כפרה דאי אמרת לאחר שנתכפרו ירעה גזרה שמא יאמרו קודם שנתכפרו בששניהם עומדים (אחד מהן ירעה) [אחד לכפרה ואחד לרעייה] והיה מפריש לרעייה קודם שיתכפר באחר וזה אינו דין שכיון שהוא מחויב להביא אשמו ושניהם ראויים לאשם לא ירעה האחד עד שיתכפר בחברו משום הכי קאמר ימות:
notes.en: As, had it taught us: only one, a guilt offering whose owner died or achieved atonement, in this Rabbi Eliezer says they die because he decreed after atonement on account of before atonement. For if you say that after they achieved atonement it grazes, there is a decree lest people say [the same] before they achieved atonement, when both are standing, [one for atonement and one for grazing], and he would set one aside for grazing before he achieved atonement with the other. That is not proper: since he is obligated to bring his guilt offering and both are fit for a guilt offering, he should not leave one to graze until he has achieved atonement with its fellow. That is why he says it dies.

messages.text: If burnt offerings were brought with the money from the sale in a case where the owner already achieved atonement by means of another offering, people might mistakenly say that if a guilt offering was lost and another was designated in its place, there too the other animal is sold and burnt offerings are brought from the proceeds. In fact, in that case, as atonement has not yet been achieved, that money must actually be used for a guilt offering.

But with regard to the substitute of a guilt offering and the offspring of its substitute, which in any case are sent to graze, even if the owner did not achieve atonement with another animal, one might say that Rabbi Eliezer concedes to the Rabbis, as there is no need for such a decree.

notes.he: דליכא למימר הכי דהא קודם כפרה נמי תמורת אשם לאו להקרבה קיימא דהכי הוא דגמירי לה:
notes.en: But the substitute of a guilt offering: where one cannot say this, for even before atonement the substitute of a guilt offering does not stand to be sacrificed, as that is how it is learned [as a tradition].

notes.he: רבי אליעזר דרועה. ע"א ירושלמי דאי אשמעינן גבי תמורה בההיא קאמר ר' אליעזר תמות היא וולדותיה משום דאתי לאיחלופי הואיל ושתיהן עומדות ההקדש והתמורה אתי לטעות ולהחליף הראשון לרעייה והתמורה לאשם הואיל וסוף סוף דמיה קרבי לא איכפת ליה אי מקריב לה וקעבד תרי איסורי חדא דמקריב התמורה ועוד דמייתי בדמי האשם עולה והוא לא נתכפר עדיין דתמורה לא כיפרה לו כדאמרינן לקמן דאין דבר הבא בעבירה מכפר על חטא ותמורה באה בעבירה שעבר על לא יחליפנו אבל אשם שכפרו בעליו דלא אתי לאיחלופי דהא אם נמצא ראשון קודם כפרת שני לא איכפת לן הי קריב והי רועה אימא מודה להו לרבנן כו':
notes.en: Say he concedes: Rabbi Eliezer [concedes] that it grazes. Another explanation, a Jerusalem version: had it taught us about a substitute, in that case Rabbi Eliezer says that it and its offspring die because they might be confused. Since both are standing, the consecrated animal and the substitute, one might err and exchange them, leaving the first to graze and taking the substitute for the guilt offering; since in the end its money is sacrificed, he would not care whether he sacrifices it, and he would commit two prohibitions: one, that he sacrifices the substitute, and further, that he brings a burnt offering with the money of the guilt offering when he has not yet achieved atonement, since the substitute does not atone for him, as we say below that an item that comes from a transgression does not atone for a sin, and a substitute comes from a transgression, as he transgressed “He shall not exchange it.” But a guilt offering whose owners achieved atonement will not be confused, for if the first was found before the second achieved atonement we do not care which is sacrificed and which grazes; so one might say that he concedes to the Rabbis etc.

notes.dh: אבל גבי תמורת אשם ולד תמורה
notes.he: דהכא ליכא למיגזר דלעולם דינו ירעו בין לפני כפרה בין לאחר כפרה אימא מודי להו לרבנן דירעו צריכא למימר נמי בהא ימותו דגזר הני אטו הני אשם שמתו ושכפרו:
notes.en: But with regard to the substitute of a guilt offering and the offspring of the substitute: here there is nothing to decree, since its law is always to graze, whether before atonement or after atonement. One might say that he concedes to the Rabbis that they graze; it is necessary to state that here too [he says] they die, for he decreed these on account of those, a guilt offering whose owners died or achieved atonement.

messages.text: And had the tanna taught us the dispute only there, in the case of the substitute of a guilt offering and the offspring of the substitute, I might have said that perhaps it is only in this case that the Rabbis say the animals are sent to graze, as there is no reason for a decree. But with regard to the case of a guilt offering where the owners achieved atonement, one might say that they concede to Rabbi Eliezer that the animals are left to die, as a decree. Therefore, both cases are necessary.

notes.he: ל"א דאי תנא תמורת אשם לחוד דהיינו בבא קמייתא הוה אמינא התם דפליגי רבנן משום דאתי לאיחלופי דאי אמרת תמורת אשם ימות גזרה שמא יתחלף לו באשם עצמו וימות האשם עצמו הילכך קאמרי [ירעו] דאם יתחלפו לכשירגיש אית ליה תקנה ויחזור ויביאנו ויקריבנו אבל בתרייתא באשם שמתו בעלים או נתכפרו דהכא ליכא חלוף (דלא הוי) [דהא לא הוי] אלא חד אשם אימא לא פליגי אלא [קסברי] ימות להכי תנא בתרייתא דבהא נמי פליגי (דפליגי בהא אטו רישא) ואי תנא אשם שמתו בהא אמר ר' אלעזר ימות משום דלא מיחלף דליכא אחר אבל תמורת אשם כו':
notes.en: Another version: had he taught only the substitute of a guilt offering, which is the first clause, I would have said that there the Rabbis disagree because it might be exchanged: for if you say the substitute of a guilt offering dies, there is a decree lest it be exchanged for the guilt offering itself and the guilt offering itself be left to die. Therefore they say [it grazes], for if they are exchanged, when he notices he has a remedy: he can go back, bring it and sacrifice it. But in the latter clause, a guilt offering whose owners died or achieved atonement, there is no exchange, [since there is] only one guilt offering; I would say they do not disagree but [hold] it dies. That is why he taught the latter clause, to show that here too they disagree. And had he taught [only] a guilt offering whose owners died, in this Rabbi Elazar [so the text; the sense seems to require Rabbi Eliezer] says it dies, because it cannot be exchanged, as there is no other; but the substitute of a guilt offering etc.

messages.text: This dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis with regard to the offspring of a substitute applies only after atonement has been achieved, i.e., after the guilt offering has been sacrificed. But before atonement is achieved, and the consecrated animal and the substitute are both present, everyone agrees that even the offspring itself is sacrificed as a guilt offering, if the owner wishes.

notes.he: ולד התמורה יקרב אשם אם אבד הראשון:
notes.en: It itself: the offspring of the substitute is sacrificed as a guilt offering, if the first was lost.

notes.dh: אבל לפני כפרה ד"ה הוא עצמו יקרב אשם
notes.he: וא"ת וכי עדיף האי ולד מאימיה דאילו אימיה אינה קריבה אשם דהלכה למשה מסיני דתמורת אשם אינה קריבה אשם וי"ל דשמא סבירא ליה דתמורת אשם כיון דנקבה היא שפיר קריבה אשם לפני כפרה דלא איגמר הילכתא אלא בתמורה דהיא עצמה חזיא לאשם כגון זכר אבל לאחר כפרה כל מותרות לנדבה אזלי ובתר הכי קאמר מחלוקת לפני כפרה שהתמורה נמי דמיה קריבה לעולה ס"ל:
notes.en: But before atonement, everyone agrees that it itself is sacrificed as a guilt offering: And if you say: is this offspring better than its mother? Its mother is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, since it is a halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai that the substitute of a guilt offering is not sacrificed as a guilt offering. One can say that perhaps he holds that where the substitute of a guilt offering is female, [its offspring] may indeed be sacrificed as a guilt offering before atonement, since the halakha was learned only about a substitute that is itself fit for a guilt offering, such as a male; but after atonement all leftovers go to gift offerings. And afterward, when he says “the dispute is before atonement,” he holds that the substitute too, its money is sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.he: דולד תמורת אשם דלרבנן ירעה ולר' אלעזר יביא בדמיו עולה אלא לאחר כפרה לאחר שנתכפר באשם עצמו ונשתייר זה:
notes.en: Not taught: that [the dispute about] the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering, which according to the Rabbis grazes and according to Rabbi Elazar he brings a burnt offering with its money, [applies] only after atonement, after he achieved atonement with the guilt offering itself and this one remained.

notes.he: אם עדיין לא נתכפר בו והרי שניהם עומדים האשם עצמו וולד תמורתו:
notes.en: But before atonement: if he has not yet achieved atonement with it, and both are standing, the guilt offering itself and the offspring of its substitute.

notes.he: הולד עצמו אם ירצה (קרב אשם) [להקריבו לאשם יקריב] שיכול הוא להתכפר באיזה שירצה ששניהם זכרים הם:
notes.en: Everyone agrees that it itself: the offspring itself, if he wishes [to sacrifice it as a guilt offering, he may sacrifice it], for he can achieve atonement with whichever he wishes, since both are males.

messages.text: There are two refutations of this statement: One is that a person cannot achieve atonement through an item that comes from a transgression, and this offspring comes from a transgression, as its mother was rendered a substitute, which is prohibited.
messages.quote: everyone agrees that even the offspring itself is sacrificed as a guilt offering

notes.he: ותמורה עבר על לא יחליפנו (ויקרא כז) ואע"ג דתמורת עולה ושלמים קרבה הנהו לאו לכפרה אתיין:
notes.en: Through a transgression: for with a substitute he transgressed “He shall not exchange it” (Leviticus 27:10). And although the substitute of a burnt offering and of a peace offering is sacrificed, those do not come for atonement.

notes.dh: אין אדם מתכפר בדבר הבא בעבירה
notes.he: ותמורה באה בעבירה היא שעבר על לא יחליפנו ואע"ג דתמורת עולה ושלמים קריבה הנהו לאו לכפרה אתיין לשון רש"י:
notes.en: A person cannot achieve atonement through an item that comes from a transgression: and a substitute comes from a transgression, as he transgressed “He shall not exchange it.” And although the substitute of a burnt offering and of a peace offering is sacrificed, those do not come for atonement. [This is] Rashi’s wording.

notes.dh: אמר רבא שתי תשובות בדבר [חדא דאין אדם מתכפר
notes.he: בשבח הקדש בדבר הבא בעבירה דולד זה בא מתמורה שבאה בעבירה דהא כתיב לא ימיר אותו:
notes.en: Rava said: There are two refutations of the matter: [One, that a person cannot achieve atonement] with the increment of consecrated property through an item that comes from a transgression, for this offspring comes from a substitute, which came through a transgression, as it is written: “He shall not exchange it.”

messages.text: And in addition, didn’t Rav Ḥananya teach a baraita in support of the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who said that only the first offspring of a peace offering is sacrificed, but the second offspring, i.e., the offspring of the offspring, is not sacrificed? Here too, the offspring of a substitute is considered like the second offspring, as it is two stages removed from the original offering.

notes.dh: ורב חנינא לסיועי לר' יהושע בן לוי
notes.he: לעיל בהאי פירקא (תמורה דף יח:):
notes.en: And Rav Ḥananya [taught] in support of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi [Rashi’s heading reads “Rav Ḥanina”]: above in this chapter (Temurah 18b).

notes.he: והאי ולד שני הוא דתמורה קרי וולד הואיל ומכח אחר אתי:
notes.en: The second offspring is not sacrificed: and this is a second offspring, since he calls the substitute an offspring, as it comes by the force of another.

notes.he: ולד תמורה כולד שני דמי והקשה מורי הרמ"ר מאי קפריך והא רבי יהושע ב"ל אליבא דרבי שמעון קאמר ופליגי רבנן עליה דכל ולדות קרבי עד סוף העולם ותירץ דפריך אהא דקאמר ד"ה ואפילו כר' אליעזר ואיהו דקאמר אפילו לרבנן ולד ראשון קרב ולד שני אינו קרב אלמא גרע שני מראשון וא"כ לר' אליעזר דאמר במתני' ולד ראשון אינו קרב כ"ש שני:
notes.en: The second offspring is not sacrificed: the offspring of a substitute is like a second offspring. My teacher, the Ramar, asked: what is the objection? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi spoke according to Rabbi Shimon, and the Rabbis disagree with him, holding that all offspring are sacrificed until the end of the world. And he answered that the objection is to his saying “everyone agrees,” even Rabbi Eliezer. And [Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi] says that even according to the Rabbis the first offspring is sacrificed and the second offspring is not; evidently the second is inferior to the first. If so, according to Rabbi Eliezer, who says in the mishna that the first offspring is not sacrificed, all the more so the second.

notes.he: בריש פירקין ולד שני אינו קרב והאי ולד תמורה היינו ולד שני דתמורה עצמה הוי ולד ראשון דאתיא מכח הזבח אלא אי אתמר הכי אתמר]:
notes.en: And in addition, didn’t Rav Ḥananya teach: at the beginning of our chapter, that the second offspring is not sacrificed? And this offspring of a substitute is a second offspring, for the substitute itself is a first offspring, since it comes by the force of the offering. Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this.]

messages.text: The dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis with regard to the offspring of a substitute applies only before atonement has been achieved, as Rabbi Eliezer holds that it is left to die, due to a concern that it might be sacrificed as a guilt offering, whereas the Rabbis say that it is left to graze, as there is no concern that it will be brought as a guilt offering. But after the original guilt offering is sacrificed and atonement has been achieved, everyone agrees that even the offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering, as there is no further concern that it might be sacrificed as a guilt offering.
messages.lead: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this: Rav Naḥman says that Rabba bar Avuh says:

notes.he: דולד תמורה קודם כפרה דהתם אמר ר"א ימות דאי אמרת ירעה כיון דדמיה קרבי אתי לאיחלופי ולאקרוביה לאשם ורבנן אמרי כיון דאיהו גופיה לא אקריב עולה לא אתי לאיחלופי אבל לאחר כפרה דליכא למימר איחלופי הוא והולד עצמו יקרב עולה:
notes.en: The dispute: about the offspring of a substitute before atonement. There Rabbi Eliezer said it dies, for if you say it grazes, since its money is sacrificed, they would come to confuse it and sacrifice it as a guilt offering; and the Rabbis say that since it itself is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, they would not come to confuse it. But after atonement, where one cannot speak of confusion, the offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.he: דפליגי רבנן ור' אלעזר אלא לפני כפרה דלפני כפרה לא מצי להקריב אשם דאין אדם מתכפר בדבר הבא בעבירה:
notes.en: Not taught: that the Rabbis and Rabbi Elazar disagree except before atonement, for before atonement he cannot sacrifice it as a guilt offering, as a person cannot achieve atonement through an item that comes from a transgression.

messages.text: But didn’t Rav Ḥananya teach a baraita in support of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that the second offspring is not sacrificed? How, then, can the offspring of the substitute be sacrificed, as it too should be treated like the second offspring?
messages.quote: everyone agrees that even the offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering

messages.text: That is difficult.

notes.dh: אבל לאחר כפרה דברי הכל ולד עצמו קרב עולה
notes.he: דעולה לאו לכפרה אתיא. והא תאני רב חנניא [לסיועיה] דולד שני אינו קרב כלל קשיא:
notes.en: But after atonement, everyone agrees that the offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering, for a burnt offering does not come for atonement. But didn’t Rav Ḥananya teach [in support] that the second offspring is not sacrificed at all? It is difficult.

notes.dh: ל"א דברי הכל ולד קרב אשם
notes.he: אמר רבא ב' תשובות כו'. ועוד הא תאני כו'. אלא אימא יביא בדמיו עולה לנדבת יחיד דולד שני אינו קרב איכא דאמרי לא שנו דפליגי אלא לפני כפרה דרבנן סברי האי ולד הוי מותר אשם וירעה ויפלו דמיו לנדבה ור' אלעזר סבר לנדבת יחיד אבל לאחר כפרה כיון (דהוי) דזכר הוא וחזי להקרבה קא סברי דיקרב עצמו עולה והתני רב חנניא כו'. אלא אימא יביא בדמיו של ולד שני עולה דאיכא שם עולה:
notes.en: Another version: “Everyone agrees that the offspring is sacrificed as a guilt offering.” Rava said: Two refutations etc. And in addition, didn’t he teach etc. Rather, say: he brings a burnt offering with its money as an individual’s gift offering, since the second offspring is not sacrificed. Some say: they disagree only before atonement, for the Rabbis hold that this offspring is a leftover guilt offering, which grazes and its money is allocated for gift offerings, and Rabbi Elazar holds [it is] for an individual’s gift offering; but after atonement, since it is male and fit for sacrifice, they hold that it itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering. But didn’t Rav Ḥananya teach etc. Rather, say: he brings a burnt offering with the money of the second offspring, since there is burnt offering status [on it].

messages.text: @Rabbi Avin bar Kahana If one designated a female animal as a guilt offering and it gave birth to a male, what is the halakha with regard to whether its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering?
messages.lead: § Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya inquired of Rabbi Avin bar Kahana:

messages.text: And let him resolve the inquiry from the statement of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, who said that Rabbi Elazar concedes that if one designates a female animal as a guilt offering, the offspring is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, as there is no guilt offering status for animals that are the same sex as the mother, and likewise it is not sacrificed as a burnt offering, as the mother was designated as a guilt offering.
messages.quote: what is the halakha with regard to whether its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering?

notes.he: לעיל מודה ר"א כו' ושמעינן מינה דטעמיה דרבי אליעזר גבי ולד מפריש נקבה לעולה משום דאיכא שם עולה על אמו אבל הכא דליכא שם עולה על אמו לא:
notes.en: From Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, who said: above, “Rabbi Elazar concedes etc.” And we learn from it that the reason of Rabbi Eliezer [so Rashi’s text; the statement above is Rabbi Elazar’s] with regard to the offspring of one who designates a female for a burnt offering is that there is burnt offering status on its mother; but here, where there is no burnt offering status on its mother, it is not so.

notes.dh: ותפשוט ליה מדר' יוסי בר חנינא דאמר לעיל
notes.he: ומודי ר' אלעזר במפריש נקבה לאשם:
notes.en: And let him resolve it from Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina, who said above: Rabbi Elazar concedes with regard to one who designates a female for a guilt offering.

messages.text: Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya never heard that statement of Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina.

notes.he: לא למדה מעולם (רב כהנא זו) [ר' אבין בר חייא]. ומודי ר' אלעזר. מאי כלומר מאי אהדריה רבין בר כהנא:
notes.en: He never heard it: [Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya] never learned it [the text has “Rav Kahana”, corrected in brackets]. “Rabbi Elazar concedes.” “What”: that is, what did Ravin bar Kahana answer him?

messages.text: The Gemara returns to the inquiry of Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya: What is the halakha?
Its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering.
messages.lead: Rabbi Avin bar Kahana said to Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya:

messages.text: What is this? Rabbi Elazar says in the mishna (18b) that the offspring itself is offered as a burnt offering only when he designates a female animal as a burnt offering and then it gives birth to a male, due to the fact that there is burnt offering status for a bird that is the same sex as its mother. But with regard to a female animal that was designated as a guilt offering and subsequently gave birth to a male, where there is no guilt offering status for animals that are the same sex as its mother, even Rabbi Eliezer concedes that its offspring is not sacrificed at all.
messages.lead: Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya challenges his response:
messages.quote: Its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.dh: אבל גבי אשם דליכא שם עולה על אמו
notes.he: הכא לא מצי לפרושי דליכא שם עולה על אמו בעולת העוף דהא הוי שם עולה על אמו בעולת העוף אלא ה"פ תחילת הקדש דאימיה לאו לשם עולה איקדיש דהא לשם אשם הוקדש:
notes.en: But with regard to a guilt offering, where there is no burnt offering status on its mother: Here one cannot explain that there is no burnt offering status on its mother from the bird burnt offering, since there is burnt offering status on its mother from the bird burnt offering. Rather, this is the explanation: the initial consecration of its mother was not as a burnt offering, for it was consecrated as a guilt offering.

notes.he: עד כאן לא קאמר רבי אלעזר בנה קרב עולה אלא גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה דאיכא שם עולה על נקבה אבל גבי אשם דליכא שם אשם על נקבה מודי דאין בנה קרב עולה:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar says that its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering only with regard to one who designates a female for a burnt offering, where there is burnt offering status for a female; but with regard to a guilt offering, where there is no guilt offering status for a female, he concedes that its offspring is not sacrificed as a burnt offering. [Rabbeinu Gershom has Rabbi Elazar himself concede, where the printed text reads “even Rabbi Eliezer concedes”.]

messages.text: The reason for the statement of Rabbi Elazar, that the offspring of a female animal designated as a burnt offering is sacrificed as a burnt offering, is not because there is burnt offering status for an animal that is the same sex as its mother, but rather because it is fit to be sacrificed upon the altar, and this offspring of the female animal designated as a guilt offering is also fit to be sacrificed.
messages.lead: Rabbi Avin bar Kahana said to him in response:
messages.quote: that there is burnt offering status for a bird that is the same sex as its mother

notes.he: הולד:
notes.en: Because it is fit to be sacrificed: the offspring.

notes.he: א"ל טעמיה דר' אלעזר גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה דבנה קרב עולה לאו משום דשם עולה על אמו אלא משום דחזי לעולה דזכר הוא והאי נמי בנה של אשם זכר הוא וחזי לעולה:
notes.en: He said to him: The reason of Rabbi Elazar, with one who designates a female for a burnt offering, that its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering, is not because there is burnt offering status on its mother but because it is fit for a burnt offering, since it is male; and this one too, the offspring of the guilt offering, is male and fit for a burnt offering.

messages.text: Rabbi Elazar says that in the case of the offspring of a female animal that was designated as a guilt offering or the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering, and the offspring of their offspring until the end of all time, they graze until they become blemished, and then they are sold, and the owner brings an individual burnt offering with the money received for their sale.
messages.lead: Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya raised an objection to Rabbi Avin bar Kahana from the mishna:
messages.quote: bring an individual burnt offering with the money received for its sale

notes.he: מתניתין היא תמורת אשם כו':
notes.en: He raised an objection: it is our mishna, “The substitute of a guilt offering etc.”

notes.he: מילתיה דרבי אלעזר נקט:
notes.en: He brings a burnt offering with their money: he cited the statement of Rabbi Elazar.

messages.text: With the money received for their sale, yes, he brings a burnt offering,

notes.he: ותימה למורי הרמ"ר מאי קפריך היינו טעמא דהכא הוא עצמו לא משום דאתי לאיחלופי כדאיתא לעיל והאי טעמא לא שייך במפריש נקבה לאשם ותי' דנ"ל דלא אמר הני טעמי דלעיל אלא לגבי התמורה עצמו אבל הולד יש לו דחיית אמו והיכי קאמרת במפריש נקבה לאשם דבנה עצמה יקרב עולה וה"נ אנו צ"ל לעיל בפירקין (דצ"ל) דפריך מהאי משנה דהכא לר"א דאמר המפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה הוא עצמו יקרב עולה:
notes.en: With their money, yes; themselves, no: My teacher, the Ramar, found this puzzling: what is the objection? The reason that here [the offspring] itself is not sacrificed is that it might be confused, as stated above, and that reason does not apply to one who designates a female for a guilt offering. And he answered that it seems to him that those reasons above were said only about the substitute itself, but the offspring carries the rejection of its mother; so how can you say, with one who designates a female for a guilt offering, that its offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering? And so too we must say above in our chapter, that he objects from this mishna here to Rabbi Elazar, who says: One who designates a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth, it itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering.

messages.text: Continues on 21a: “but the offspring itself, no.” Rabbi Avin bar Kahana answers that the mishna is speaking of a female that gave birth to a female.
